notes.title: The Skyrim civil war
notes.text: Skyrim is at war with itself: Ulfric Stormcloak's rebels fight for independence and the return of Talos worship, while General Tullius's Imperial Legion fights to keep Skyrim in the Empire. The holds are split, and ordinary folk suffer raids, high prices and divided families.

notes.title: Who backs whom in the war
notes.text: When the war began, Haafingar, the Reach, Falkreath and Hjaalmarch backed the Empire, while Eastmarch, the Rift, the Pale and Winterhold backed Ulfric. Whiterun, at the center, stayed neutral, and both sides know whoever holds Whiterun holds Skyrim.

notes.title: The Great War
notes.text: The Great War (4E 171-175) pitted the Empire against the Aldmeri Dominion. The Thalmor sacked the Imperial City; Emperor Titus Mede II retook it at the Battle of the Red Ring, but the exhausted Empire then made peace on humiliating terms. Many Skyrim veterans remember it bitterly.

notes.title: The White-Gold Concordat
notes.text: The White-Gold Concordat ended the Great War. The Empire gave up southern Hammerfell, disbanded the Blades, outlawed Talos worship and let Thalmor Justiciars enforce the ban. Many Nords see it as betrayal, and it is the root of Ulfric's rebellion.

notes.title: The Markarth Incident
notes.text: In 4E 176 the Forsworn seized the Reach and held Markarth for two years. Ulfric Stormcloak's militia retook it on the promise that Talos worship would be allowed. When the Thalmor found out, they demanded Ulfric's arrest, and the broken promise turned Ulfric against the Empire.

notes.title: The death of High King Torygg
notes.text: Ulfric Stormcloak challenged High King Torygg to a duel in the Blue Palace and killed him with his Voice. Ulfric's followers call it an honorable challenge by ancient custom; Imperials and Torygg's widow Elisif call it murder. It sparked the open civil war.

notes.title: The Moot and the High Kingship
notes.text: Skyrim's High King is chosen by the Moot, a council of all the Jarls. Since Torygg's death no Moot has been called: the Empire favors his widow Elisif, while Ulfric claims the crown for himself.

notes.title: The attack on Helgen
notes.text: Word has spread that Helgen was destroyed by a dragon in the middle of Ulfric's execution, and that Ulfric escaped in the chaos. Many dismiss it as wild rumor; others fear the old tales are coming true.

notes.title: The return of the dragons
notes.text: Dragons had not been seen in Skyrim for thousands of years, but now they are attacking towns and travellers. People argue whether it is an omen of the end times, punishment for abandoning Talos, or something worse.

notes.title: Alduin's return
notes.text: The black dragon seen at Helgen is Alduin the World-Eater himself, returned from beyond time. He flies across Skyrim raising the dead dragons from their burial mounds, and he devours souls in Sovngarde to grow stronger.

notes.title: The Dragon War
notes.text: Long ago the ancient Nords rose up against the dragons who ruled them. Taught the Thu'um by Kyne's grace, their heroes fought Alduin on the Throat of the World, and legend says they cast him out of time with an Elder Scroll.

notes.title: The Red Year
notes.text: In 4E 5 Red Mountain on Vvardenfell erupted, devastating Morrowind, and the Argonians soon invaded its south. Waves of Dunmer refugees fled to Skyrim and Solstheim, and their descendants are still treated as outsiders.

notes.title: The Oblivion Crisis
notes.text: About two hundred years ago, gates to Oblivion opened across Tamriel and Mehrunes Dagon's armies poured through. Martin Septim, the last of his line, sacrificed himself to stop it, ending the Third Era and the Septim dynasty.

notes.title: The Great Collapse
notes.text: In 4E 122 a terrible storm and series of collapses sent most of the city of Winterhold into the sea, yet the College's tower was untouched. Locals have blamed the mages ever since, though the College denies any part in it.

notes.title: Ysgramor and the Five Hundred
notes.text: Ysgramor is the legendary first king of the Nords. After elves massacred his people at Saarthal in the Night of Tears, he sailed back from Atmora with five hundred companions and drove the Snow Elves from Skyrim. The Companions of Whiterun claim him as their founder.

notes.title: Tiber Septim
notes.text: Tiber Septim, born Hjalti Early-Beard and called Talos, was the Dragonborn general who united all of Tamriel into the Third Empire. After death he ascended to become the Ninth Divine, which is why Nords hold him so dear.

notes.title: Akavir and the Akaviri
notes.text: Akavir is a mysterious continent east of Tamriel whose peoples invaded several times long ago. The Akaviri who stayed and served the Dragonborn emperors became the Dragonguard, forerunners of the Blades; their curved swords are still called Akaviri blades.

notes.title: Thalmor schemes in Skyrim
notes.text: Secret Thalmor papers reveal they want Skyrim's civil war to drag on, weakening both the Empire and the Nords, and they consider Ulfric a useful, if unwitting, asset since his capture during the Great War.
